proposals.before: At the end of Zhenguang, Minister of Works Li Chong was made regional commander of the commandery and led forces against the Rouran, with Langen as his chief clerk.
proposals.after: At the end of Zhenguang, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Li Chong was made regional commander of the commandery and led forces against the Rouran, with Langen as his chief clerk.
proposals.reason: Chinese 尚書令 is Director/Prefect of the Masters of Writing, not Minister of Works (司空).

proposals.before: At the end of Zhenguang, Minister of Works Li Chong was made Regional Commander of the commandery and led forces against the Rouran, with Langen as chief clerk.
proposals.after: At the end of Zhenguang, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Li Chong was made Regional Commander of the commandery and led forces against the Rouran, with Langen as chief clerk.
proposals.reason: Chinese 尚書令 is mistranslated as Minister of Works.

proposals.before: Chong reported it up to Qin; the matter rested without response.
proposals.after: Chong reported it upward in a memorial; the matter rested without response.
proposals.reason: 秦聞 is a corruption/misreading of 奏聞 'report upward'; Qin is not a place or addressee here.

proposals.before: At the time Wang Daoxi, attendant respondant to edicts, enjoyed Zhuang's trust. Langen attached himself to him, seeking merit in the field.
proposals.after: At the time Wang Daoxi, attendant respondent to edicts, enjoyed Zhuang's trust. Langen attached himself to him, seeking merit in the field.
proposals.reason: English typo: respondant should be respondent.

proposals.before: At the time, Attendant Respondant to Edicts Wang Daoxi enjoyed Zhuang's trust; Langen attached himself to him, seeking to win merit abroad.
proposals.after: At the time, Attendant Respondent to Edicts Wang Daoxi enjoyed Zhuang's trust; Langen attached himself to him, seeking to win merit abroad.
proposals.reason: English typo: Respondant should be Respondent.

proposals.before: Gao Huan, with no choice, thereupon enthroned Emperor Wucheng.
proposals.after: Gao Huan, with no choice, thereupon enthroned Emperor Wu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 武帝 is Emperor Wu; Wucheng would be 武成.

proposals.before: The deposed emperor had long possessed virtue and achievement, yet because Langen and others framed and defamed him, he was deeply censured by contemporary opinion.
proposals.after: The deposed emperor had long possessed virtue and achievement, yet because Langen and others framed and defamed him, they were deeply censured by contemporary opinion.
proposals.reason: Subject of 深為時論所非 is Langen and the others who framed him, not the deposed emperor.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Taichang he was made equal in protocol to three imperators, soon additionally opener of a government office, and enfeoffed marquis of Julu County with seven hundred households.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Taichang he was made equal in protocol to the Three Dukes, soon additionally opener of a government office, and enfeoffed marquis of Julu County with seven hundred households.
proposals.reason: 三司 denotes the Three Dukes; “three imperators” is a clear mistranslation.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Taichang he was made Equal in Protocol to Three Imperators, soon additionally Opener of a Government Office, enfeoffed Marquis of Julu County with a fief of seven hundred households.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Taichang he was made Equal in Protocol to the Three Dukes, soon additionally Opener of a Government Office, enfeoffed Marquis of Julu County with a fief of seven hundred households.
proposals.reason: 三司 denotes the Three Dukes; “Three Imperators” is a clear mistranslation.

proposals.before: Emperor Wucheng severely condemned him. Langen, terrified, cited illness and resigned as vice director.
proposals.after: Emperor Wu severely condemned him. Langen, terrified, cited illness and resigned as vice director.
proposals.reason: 武帝 is Emperor Wu; “Wucheng” renders 武成, a different imperial name.

proposals.before: Posthumously granted supervisor of military affairs in Ji, Ding, and Yin provinces, inspector of Ding Province, duke over the masses, and palace attendant, with the posthumous title Wenzuan.
proposals.after: Posthumously granted supervisor of military affairs in Ji, Ding, and Yin provinces, inspector of Ding Province, duke over the masses, and palace attendant, with the posthumous title Wenxuan.
proposals.reason: 文宣 is Wenxuan, not Wenzuan.

proposals.before: Posthumously granted supervisor of military affairs in the three provinces of Ji, Ding, and Yin, Inspector of Ding Province, Duke over the Masses, Palace Attendant, with posthumous title Wenzuan.
proposals.after: Posthumously granted supervisor of military affairs in the three provinces of Ji, Ding, and Yin, Inspector of Ding Province, Duke over the Masses, Palace Attendant, with posthumous title Wenxuan.
proposals.reason: 文宣 is Wenxuan, not Wenzuan.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Wuping he served as palace investigating censor, then was transferred to secretariat attendant and awaited edicts at the Wulin Hall.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Wuping he served as palace investigating censor, then was transferred to secretariat attendant and awaited edicts at the Wenlin Hall.
proposals.reason: 文林館 is Wenlin Hall, not Wulin Hall.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Wuping he was palace investigating censor; he was transferred to attendant of the Secretariat and awaited edicts at the Wulin Hall.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Wuping he was palace investigating censor; he was transferred to attendant of the Secretariat and awaited edicts at the Wenlin Hall.
proposals.reason: 文林館 is Wenlin Hall, not Wulin Hall.

proposals.before: Soon he was removed and made attendant of the Yellow Gate; he was transferred to general and right grand master for splendid happiness.
proposals.after: Soon he was appointed attendant of the Yellow Gate; he was transferred to general and right grand master for splendid happiness.
proposals.reason: 除 here means appointment to office, not removal; the literal 'removed and made' reverses the sense of 尋除.

proposals.before: Soon he was removed and made governor of Xu Province; he was given three hundred retainers of Guangzong and a thousand retainers of Qinghe.
proposals.after: Soon he was appointed governor of Xu Province; he was given three hundred retainers of Guangzong and a thousand retainers of Qinghe.
proposals.reason: 除 means to appoint; 'removed and made' mistranslates 尋除徐州刺史.

proposals.before: Ling was by nature arrogant and overbearing; he favored his concubine Lady Feng and lent her his punitive authority, taking and accepting as she pleased — government and customs were not established.
proposals.after: Ling was by nature arrogant and overbearing; he favored his concubine Lady Feng and lent her his punitive authority, so she extorted and accepted bribes at will — government and customs were not established.
proposals.reason: 恣情取受 is Lady Feng's conduct under borrowed authority; the literal leaves the subject ambiguous and omits the extortion sense.

proposals.before: When Shou went on a mission to hire Liang and passed through Xu Province, Ling equipped the full insignia of a governor to escort him and had a man convey word to Wei: "Do not wonder at the many guards — it is the power of classical learning."
proposals.after: When Shou went on a mission to Liang and passed through Xu Province, Ling equipped the full insignia of a governor to escort him and had a man convey word to Wei: "Do not wonder at the many guards — it is the power of classical learning."
proposals.reason: 聘梁 is a diplomatic mission to Liang, not 'hire Liang'.

proposals.before: Cui Xian's cousin by marriage Li Shen heard of it.
proposals.after: Li Shen, Cui Xian's cousin by marriage, then [took it up].
proposals.reason: Chinese ends abruptly at 以; English invents 'heard of it,' which is not in the truncated clause 暹外兄李慎以。

proposals.before: Cui Xian's cousin by marriage Li Shen heard of it.
proposals.after: Li Shen, Cui Xian's cousin by marriage, then [took it up].
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise invents 'heard of it' for truncated 暹外兄李慎以。

proposals.before: To supply a worthy enemy with a talented man is not fitting."
proposals.after: To supply the enemy with a man of talent is not fitting."
proposals.reason: 英賢 is the talented man supplied; 寇敵 is the enemy. The literal reverses the roles.

proposals.before: Cui Xian was commandant of justice; he memorialized to appoint Zhan censor — he was taken in for talent and reputation, which Xian did not favor.
proposals.after: Cui Xian was commandant of justice; he memorialized to appoint Zhan censor — he was taken in for talent and reputation, which was not to Zhan's liking.
proposals.reason: 非其好也 refers to Zhan's preference, not Cui Xian's; the censor post was not what Zhan desired.

proposals.before: Cui Xian was commandant of justice; he memorialized to remove [Zhan] as censor — he was taken in for talent and reputation, which was not to Xian's liking.
proposals.after: Cui Xian was commandant of justice; he memorialized to appoint [Zhan] as censor — he was taken in for talent and reputation, which was not to his (Zhan's) liking.
proposals.reason: 除 here means appoint, not remove; 非其好也 refers to Zhan, not Xian.

proposals.before: With Li Gai of Zhao Commandery he was a friend of no opposition.
proposals.after: With Li Gai of Zhao Commandery he was an intimate friend of complete accord.
proposals.reason: 莫逆之友 means intimate friends in perfect accord; 'friend of no opposition' is an opaque calque.

proposals.before: He helped fix the Five Rites and awaited orders at the Wulin Hall.
proposals.after: He helped fix the Five Rites and awaited orders at the Forest of Letters Hall.
proposals.reason: 文林館 is the Forest of Letters Hall (Wenlin), not Wulin.

proposals.before: Ling's clansman Zhaoshi was grandson of Wei, vice director of the masters of writing Liang.
proposals.after: Ling's clansman Zhaoshi was grandson of Wei Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liang.
proposals.reason: The comma after Wei wrongly treats Wei as a person; 魏 modifies the Northern Wei office of Liang.

proposals.before: When he reached the border of Qi Province, local bandits led by Cui Kumarajiva seized him.
proposals.after: When he reached the border of Qi Province, local bandits led by Cui Jiaye seized him and wanted to force him to join them.
proposals.reason: 迦葉 is Jiaye (Kāśyapa), not Kumarajiva; idiomatic also omits 欲逼與同事.

proposals.before: When he reached the border of Qi Province he was captured by local bandits such as Cui Kumarajiva and others.
proposals.after: When he reached the border of Qi Province he was captured by local bandits such as Cui Jiaye and others, who wanted to force him to join them.
proposals.reason: Same wrong rendering of 迦葉 as Kumarajiva; literal also drops 欲逼與同事.

proposals.before: His son Kan, at the end of Wei also served as Unrestricted Regular Attendant and envoy on a mission to court Liang.
proposals.after: His son Kan, at the end of Wei also served as Unrestricted Regular Attendant and envoy on a mission to the Liang court.
proposals.reason: 'court Liang' reverses the modifier order of 聘梁.

proposals.before: His father Shitai was remonstrating and editing grand master.
proposals.after: His father Shitai was Remonstrance Counselor (grand master of remonstrance).
proposals.reason: 諫議大夫 is a remonstrance office; 'editing' is not in the Chinese.
